**Indikator 1** is the first and most central process indicator in the [[akut-kirurgi-databasen|Akut Kirurgi Databasen]] (AKDB), a national quality monitoring program for acute high-risk abdominal surgery in [[danmark|Denmark]] [^src1]. It measures the proportion of patients who receive [[antibiotikabehandling|antibiotic treatment]] within three hours (180 minutes) of arriving at the hospital [^src1]. The indicator relies on data from the [[sygehusmedicinregisteret|Sygehusmedicinregisteret]] to track antibiotic administration [^src2].

The clinical significance of early antibiotic administration is supported by evidence from the [[aha-studiet|AHA-studiet]] and [[elpquick|ELPQUICK]] studies, which demonstrated that early treatment is a key intervention in reducing mortality for acute abdominal surgery [^src2]. Initially, the performance standard for Indikator 1 was set at >90% [^src1]. However, national performance has consistently fallen far short of this target. For the measurement period from September 1, 2022, to August 31, 2023, the national fulfillment rate was only 30.5% [^src1]. In the subsequent period from September 1, 2023, to August 31, 2024, it improved slightly to 34.4% [^src3]. The median time from hospital arrival to antibiotic administration was 5 hours (IQR: 2–13) in the first period [^src2], and 4.4 hours nationally in the second [^src5].

Due to these persistent gaps and findings from local audits revealing that many patients are not actually septic, the steering group lowered the development target to >60% [^src4]. Despite discussions about adjusting the time limit, the three-hour threshold was maintained to balance early treatment with the need to avoid delaying crucial diagnostic procedures like [[ct-skanning|CT-skanning]] [^src4]. 

Regional and local variations in performance are significant. In the 2023–2024 period, [[region-midtjylland|Region Midtjylland]] had the highest fulfillment rate at 44.6%, while [[region-syddanmark|Region Syddanmark]] had the lowest at 22.5% [^src4]. At the hospital level, performance varied widely, with some institutions like [[bornholms-hospital|Bornholms Hospital]] achieving 63.3% in the 2022–2023 period [^src1], while others like [[odense-universitetshospital-svendborg|Odense Universitetshospital - Svendborg]] reached only 7.9% [^src1]. Quality improvement efforts, such as those led by [[lkt-akut-kirurgi|LKT Akutkirurgi]], have focused on improving the documentation of antibiotic administration [^src2], and specific hospitals like [[regionshospitalet-randers|Regionshospitalet Randers]] have shown notable progress toward the target [^src4]. The indicator's methodology and clinical relevance continue to be scrutinized, with hospitals like [[regionshospital-nordjylland|Regionshospital Nordjylland]] conducting thorough audits and questioning its applicability to specific patient subgroups [^src7]. Exclusions from the indicator's denominator include patients with invalid CPR numbers, those under 18, those not operated on, cases where preoperative antibiotic prophylaxis was not given, and patients whose surgery was not the first during their hospital stay [^src1].
